newsitem.title: UK: UK govt N.Ireland statement expected Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: UK govt N.Ireland statement expected Wednesday.

text.p: A statement to parliament by Prime Minister Tony Blair on Northern Ireland and the peace process is expected on Wednesday, a senior government official said.

Blair has been expected for some time to make a statement setting out the future path of the troubled peace negotiations and the conditions under which the Irish Republican Army's political arm, Sinn Fein, could be brought into all-party peace talks.

The official said Blair, currently in New York for a session of the United Nations earth summit, was also expected to address parliament on Tuesday on the outcome of the meeting of the Group of Seven industrialised nations in Denver which ended on Sunday.
The government has recently halted contacts between officials and Sinn Fein following the killing of two Northern Ireland policemen in an IRA ambush.
But the statement is expected to set out that Sinn Fein could be involved in all-party talks on the future of the British-ruled province weeks after the declaration of a new IRA cease-fire.
